Extract named columns from a large .xlsx by streaming its XML

Source: R/md-xlsx.R
md_xlsx_to_csv.Rd

The IRS publishes the Form 1023-EZ approvals as .xlsx only. The 2023 file is 47 MB compressed but 313 MB of sheet XML over 7.2 million string cells, and every in-process reader available here dies on it: readxl::read_excel() and DuckDB's read_xlsx() both segfault rather than erroring. Worth recording, because a segfault inside a build script reads as a crash rather than as unsupported input.

Usage

md_xlsx_to_csv(xlsx, columns = NULL, out = NULL, sheet = 1L, chunk = 20000L)

Arguments

xlsx

Path to the workbook.

columns

Header names to keep. NULL keeps everything, which is only advisable on small sheets.

out

Path to write. Defaults to the input with a .csv extension.

sheet

Sheet number within the workbook.

chunk

Rows held in memory at once.

Value

out, invisibly.

Details

So this reads the archive directly. An .xlsx is a zip; the sheet is XML with one <row> per record, and cells reference a shared string table by index.

Why it takes column names

Extracting all 70-odd columns row by row is slow enough to be unusable - the work is proportional to cells, and most of those cells are not wanted. Naming the columns turns the job into one vectorised regex per column per chunk.

It is also a disclosure control rather than only an optimisation. Columns 18-57 of the 1023-EZ approvals are five officers' personal names and home addresses. matchdb is a database of organisations; there is no reason for that data to enter it, and the cheapest way to guarantee it does not is to never parse those columns.
